Protein Food

Tri-Tip

About This Entry

Tri-tip is a triangular bottom-sirloin roast popular on the US West Coast, often Santa Maria–style grilled over oak. Moderate fat and pronounced beefiness pair with Syrah, Zinfandel, and other fruit-forward medium-to-full reds.

Beginner Guide

Tri-tip is one muscle cut into a roast or steaks. Slice against the grain — the grain changes direction in this triangular cut, which trips up many home cooks.

FAQ

What is Tri-Tip?
Tri-tip is one muscle cut into a roast or steaks.
How should Tri-Tip be cooked for best results?
Cook to medium-rare or medium depending on thickness; rest 5–10 minutes and slice against the grain when the muscle grain is visible.
